## Use this when
- monitor my software portfolio for broken products
- continuously audit all of our apps repositories and public URLs
- tell me when one of our software products breaks
- software portfolio health monitoring
- software estate integrity monitoring
- detect broken deployments and stale workflows
- watch GitHub Actions and public product doors for failures
- find drift across our apps APIs workflows and discovery surfaces
- open repair work automatically when software breaks
- continuous software estate audit
- AI product portfolio watchdog
- monitor machine readable discovery surfaces
- our company has too many apps and we do not know what is broken
- keep an inventory of all our software and verify it stays healthy
- monitor LLM discovery pages and agent endpoints
- detect product URL workflow and deployment regressions

## Problem
Organizations with growing software estates lose track of which apps, repositories, workflows, public endpoints and machine-discovery surfaces are actually healthy. Systemia Portfolio Sentinel continuously inventories known surfaces, detects material drift, deduplicates repeat failures and routes evidence-backed repair work without exposing private topology.

## Inputs
Authorized repositories, product/service inventory, public URLs, workflow metadata, machine-discovery surfaces and customer-defined monitoring boundaries. Private systems require explicit scoped authorization.

## Outputs
Current portfolio inventory, health findings, severity and change state, broken public-door/workflow detection, deduplicated repair queue, mission snapshots and evidence/receipt references.

## Pricing
Commercial pilot is custom-quoted based on portfolio size, repositories, public endpoints, workflow count and monitoring scope. No fixed public price or direct machine checkout is currently advertised.

## Invocation and authority
LIVE for public machine discovery and deterministic problem matching through Evercraft Machine Commerce. Evercraft's own Sentinel runtime is production-proven on a five-minute resident cycle; customer monitoring begins only after scoped onboarding and authorization. No discovery call grants private access or production-mutation authority.

Public discovery is read-only. Monitoring private repositories, internal systems or customer infrastructure requires explicit scoped authorization. Production changes, payment actions and external communications remain separately gated.

Payment authority: No direct machine checkout is exposed. Commercial terms and any later payment require explicit human agreement and authoritative payment verification.
